summary: Coast Guard light on Sisters Islets in the Strait of Georgia, off Lasqueti Island: lit in 1898, tower replaced in 1967, automated in 1996, closed to visitors.

structures.type: rectangular wooden dwelling with a square tower and octagonal wooden lantern
structures.note: 36 ft (11 m) from masonry foundation to the ventilator ball (LighthouseFriends). Replaced in 1967; not standing.

structures.type: narrow round cylindrical, flared at the top, with lantern and gallery
structures.note: Approx. 18 m (60 ft), painted white with a red lantern (Rowlett). Present tower.

access.note: Accessible only by boat. Site and tower closed (Rowlett); grounds and tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Marine agent James Gaudin asked for more lights for the northbound traffic and named Sisters Islets as the first place to be lit (LighthouseFriends).
Wooden lighthouse built during 1898 by George H. Frost, lowest bidder, for $3,257 (LighthouseFriends). Rowlett: station established 1898.
Placed in commission in December 1898 (LighthouseFriends). The Department's 1898 report is not in the corpus.

Fog-alarm building for a diaphone completed and the diaphone plant installed (Department report for the fiscal year ending 31 March 1908). LighthouseFriends: the plant came from the Canadian Fog Signal Company of Toronto for $1,900 and gave two three-second blasts every ninety seconds.
Fourth-order Fresnel lens installed, changing the light to a group of two flashes every ten seconds (LighthouseFriends).
Severe southeast gale over Christmas wrecked the boathouse, washed away its boatways and equipment, and damaged the walks and platforms (LighthouseFriends, keeper's report).
Slender concrete tower replaced the 1898 lighthouse, with a four-bedroom dwelling, a fog-signal building and a helicopter pad (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).
De-staffed June 1996 (LighthouseFriends). Rowlett: automated in 1996; the keeper's house is boarded up.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28. Every quote was found in its cached source on the first run (64 found, 0 missing). Corrected: (1) units now metres first, as the guide requires: 11 m (36 ft) for the 1898 tower and 14 m (46 ft) for the focal plane; (2) the opening says 'off the west end of Lasqueti Island' (Rowlett) and reports LighthouseFriends' 'northwest end' beside it; (3) Gaudin's 1897 words are quoted, not paraphrased ('the first place that should be lit', from LighthouseFriends); (4) the 1902 keeper entry is 'Sister's Rock, Vancouver' (the British Columbia district entry; the name also occurs for rocks in Ontario); (5) fiscal years: the 1907 fog-alarm report is the nine months ended 31 March 1907 (printed 1908), not 'the report for 1907'; the diaphone-completion report is the year ending 31 March 1908 (printed 1909); the 1902 list is the year ended 30 June 1902; the 1911 list is the year ending 31 March 1911; the Buss list is 1911-12; the Hayllar list is the year ending 31 March 1915. (6) Blanchard's extra salary: LighthouseFriends says his wife was 'up to the task' so the family kept the extra money; the story now says that. MATCHED BY POSITION: the 1915 Hayllar line was checked on the Internet Archive page image (printed p.83, scan 90): 'T. C. L. Hayllar' sits on the row beside 'Sisters light and fog alarm'. The 1908 'Sisters B. Blanchard' line is one printed row. The 1911 'B. Blanchard' row was checked on the page image (printed p.250, scan 257): 'Sisters' with B. Blanchard on the row below 'Sand Heads Lt. Ship' with M. O'Brien. The 1913 'Sisters W. Buss' line is one OCR row (not image-checked). BLANCHARD: LighthouseFriends ends his second stint in 1910; the Department's 1911 list still prints 'B. Blanchard' against the station; not reconciled, and the story says so. FOCAL HEIGHT: the Coast Guard list gives 24.3 m; Rowlett gives a 21 m (70 ft) focal plane; the story gives both. FIRST LIGHT 1898: LighthouseFriends and Rowlett; the 1898 report is not in the corpus. LighthouseFriends only: the 1914 lens, the 1932 gale, Lundgren's dogs, the earwigs of 1924, Elsie Tolpitt's letter, the 1967 facilities and the 1996 de-staffing (Rowlett confirms the automation). The corpus ends in 1924. POST-1960 KEEPERS: R.B. Roberts (at least 1959), Clayton Restall (1980-1984) and Ken Nelson (1985-1996) appear in the roster only as LighthouseFriends prints the list; the story does not name them. Elsie Tolpitt is not a keeper and is not in the roster. ACCESS: boat only; grounds and tower closed (Rowlett, LighthouseFriends); the story does not invite visitors. Confidence medium: the lens and gale events and the keeper dates from 1902 on rest on LighthouseFriends alone.
